entities.name: Redemptus of the Cross
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Redemptus of the Cross (Tomás Rodrigues da Cunha; d. 1638) was a Portuguese Discalced Carmelite lay brother martyred at Aceh with companions on a Portuguese mission during the height of Iberian–Acehnese conflict in the Indonesian archipelago. Sent amid diplomacy and missionary ambition, the party was executed in a climate of war and religious rivalry.

Catholic memory later venerated them among martyrs of the Indies, tying Carmelite spirituality to Portuguese Asian empire’s violent frontiers. The Aceh episode shows how evangelisation, trade, and naval power entangled in the early modern Indian Ocean.

Redemptus’s cult preserves a Carmelite martyr narrative of the Malay world.
